source: YouTube Studio analytics (28 days to 16 Nov) + per-video since-published stats for 17 Nov Shorts

channel.shorts_stayed_to_watch: 38.4% channel avg; science Shorts 30-62%, 3-question quizzes 33-42%, visual puzzles 13-29%
channel.audience: 99% new viewers; male 25-34; UK, Malaysia, Philippines, US, India

puzzle_shorts_so_far.title: Spot the Change! Can You Beat This What Changed Memory Test?
Find the Odd One Out! Only Sharp Eyes Get 3/3
Which One Doesn't Fit? Odd One Out Brain Test
What Changed? 3 Memory Puzzles Only Sharp Eyes Can Solve
Test Your Brain in 60 Seconds (text quiz)

long_videos: CTR only 2.4-2.6% (auto thumbnails) and average view duration 38-45% (1:38-1:55 of 4:13) -> custom thumbnails needed
diagnosis: Visual-puzzle Shorts lose ~80% in the first second even with hook-first. Likely causes seen in the 17 Nov s04 frames: the hook card covers puzzle panel A for the first ~3 s, the panels fill only about a third of the screen width (small emoji on a big flat background, empty bottom 40%), level 1 is EASY and each level takes ~11 s, so the Short runs 66 s. Text quizzes keep viewers better because the question is readable at once.
weak_formats: 6-level spot the difference Shorts over 1 min (13-21% stayed)
changed/memory-only openers that show nothing to solve in the first second
title-card openers (e.g. 'MEMORY GRID / 3 LEVELS' for 3 s)
best_title_patterns: Short and punchy, 3-7 words + 1-2 emoji: 'Can You Spot the Hidden Treats? 🍒🍟🍉'
Challenge stat: 'Only a few can get this right 😱🤯', '1 In 100 People Land This', 'Only 0.001% get this correct ✅'
Themed scene + task + countdown: 'Bath Time Spot The Difference — One Left!'
Direct question: 'Which is the CORRECT cup of coffee?', 'Did you get it? 👀🤔'
Keep the searchable puzzle words in the title (spot the difference, odd one out, find the…) - search is 3% of views
Avoid long, vague titles like 'What Changed? 3 Memory Puzzles Only Sharp Eyes Can Solve' (worst performer)
themes: Everyday scenes kids and adults know: bath time, breakfast table, school bag, kitchen, beach day, birthday party, toy box
Food and treats (fruits, sweets, fast food) - top niche outlier
Christmas / winter / snow (late November -> December demand rises)
Animals (zoo, farm, ocean, pets) - 'Kids vs Animal Quiz' style
Optical illusions and 'which direction is it spinning' style trick visuals
Coffee cups / correct one out of 3 (spot the correct one)
notes: Shorts traffic is 95% feed: the first frame and first second decide everything. Every Short must show the puzzle immediately; titles should promise a challenge. Long videos need custom thumbnails (upload in Studio).
